answer: Submissions that land within 299 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The grove detector writes to delta, and cedar makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 47 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
